name: pawl
description: Sixteen small deterministic checks that stop an agent from making the mistakes agents make most: sending too many messages, leaking internal paths or tokens, writing text that reads like a bot, discarding git work, running commands that wait forever, ending a turn with jobs still running, repeating the same tool call in a loop, letting test or lint counts creep up, and shipping a bug fix without a failing test first. It also auto-approves shell commands that provably only read, refuses edits that change nothing, strips zero-width characters from file writes, limits re-reads of the agent's own transcript and skill files, and asks before one conversation reads another's files. Plain Python, no model calls, no prompt cost, each check usable on its own, and a report command that tallies what they blocked. Questions: https://github.com/ulukaya/pawl/issues
suggestedPrompts: Set up a ratchet baseline for lint and test counts in this repo
Wrap my nightly cron job with the circuit breaker
Check this draft with the prose gate before I send it
